Pöbel.et: From Middle High German povel, bovel (“folk, people”, ca. 1200). Generally derived from Old French pueble, pueple. However, since Middle High German consistently shows -v-, borrowing from Italian Gallo-Romance povolo should also be considered. In any case from…

Pobolitze.et: Borrowed from Gottscheerish pobołłitsə, from Slovene povalnica.

s: Wegen ständiger Pöbelei wurde er des Raums verwiesen.
Due to constant boorishness, he was removed from the room.
Pöbelei.et: From pöbeln + -ei. Compare Schlägerei, Rauferei. The suffix “-ei” often forms abstract nouns denoting disruptive or pejorative behavior.
